name: clinicalomicsdb

relevance.justification: Directly aligned with core BioThings entity types and relations: genes (gene symbols/Ensembl IDs), drugs/treatments (NCIt-standardized oncology drugs), diseases (cancer types), and clinical trial evidence (NCT IDs, PubMed IDs), linked via quantitative drug-response statistics (p-value, AUROC, FDR) per gene per trial arm.

novelty.justification: Provides per-clinical-trial, per-gene transcriptomic drug-response association statistics (responder vs non-responder AUROC/p-value/FDR) across 40 oncology trials (5,913 patients, 11 cancer types, 67 treatment arms) — a specific data type (harmonized clinical-trial-derived pharmacogenomic response biomarkers) not itemized in mygene.info/mychem.info/mydisease.info/myvariant.info. However, the pending.api ecosystem already hosts 'Multiomics Drug Response KP' (pharmacogenomics/drug response) and 'Multiomics Clinical Trials' (clinical trials + multiomics) with closely overlapping domain descriptions; the registry does not document their underlying sources, so overlap with ClinicalOmicsDB could not be confirmed or ruled out. Novelty is scored conservatively pending that check.

openness.justification: Live-verified: public REST API (https://trials.linkedomics.org/api/) requires no login/API key and returned data via plain curl requests; per-study raw CSV files are hosted on public Box.com static links (also verified accessible without auth). License is CC BY-NC 4.0 (Oxford University Press journal license for the paper) — PASS per project policy since BioThings/Su Lab is an academic non-profit, but the NC clause is a minor risk for any downstream commercial consumers of the resulting BioThings API.

evidence.scope: Harmonized transcriptomic (gene expression, KEGG/MSigDB Hallmark/PROGENy gene-set scores, immune-cell deconvolution) data from 40 oncology clinical trials (5,913 patients, 11 cancer types, 67 treatment arms, 33 drugs) with binary responder/non-responder labels, plus precomputed gene-level and gene-set-level significance statistics (p-value, AUROC, FDR) for each study and meta-analyzed across studies per treatment.
evidence.overlap: Potential domain overlap with two already-deployed pending.api Translator KPs: 'Multiomics Drug Response KP' (pharmacogenomics/drug response) and 'Multiomics Clinical Trials' (clinical trials + multiomics). Neither entry in references/pending-api-datasources.json lists constituent source databases, so it is unconfirmed whether either already ingests ClinicalOmicsDB/LinkedOmics-derived data. No overlap found with mygene.info, mychem.info, mydisease.info, or myvariant.info source lists.

license.name: CC BY-NC 4.0
restrictions: Non-commercial use only per OUP journal license; commercial re-use requires contacting journals.permissions@oup.com

api_info.pagination: none observed; study lists returned as full arrays via POST /filter/
api_info.record_coverage: full — API exposes study metadata, per-study download links, and precomputed gene/gene-set statistics for all 40 studies

risks: Unconfirmed overlap with existing pending.api KPs 'Multiomics Drug Response KP' and 'Multiomics Clinical Trials' — their source composition is not documented in the local registry
CC BY-NC 4.0 license restricts commercial re-use; acceptable for Su Lab academic BioThings context but should be confirmed with maintainers if downstream commercial Translator consumers are a concern

Raw expression CSVs are hosted on third-party Box.com static links generated per-study by the API rather than on the datasource's own domain — link stability/staleness risk if Box links are regenerated
Disease/cancer-type field is free text (e.g. 'Kidney', 'Melanoma') without a standard ontology ID (no MONDO/DOID mapping observed) — would require a mapping step
next_actions: Confirm with pending.api maintainers whether 'Multiomics Drug Response KP' or 'Multiomics Clinical Trials' already ingest ClinicalOmicsDB/LinkedOmics data before committing to a new plugin
Proceed to Phase 3 deep inspection since relevance and openness are strong and novelty, while uncertain, is not disqualifying
